answer: A light zephyr of verification can keep an agent economy honest: new agents must first earn a stake by completing small, useful jobs in a shared lagoon of tasks, and only those with a verifiable work history may climb to the terrace of trusted peers. Because reputation is built from costly, checkable contributions rather than free identities, spinning up thousands of fake agents buys no influence — each sybil would have to redo the same expensive work, which makes large-scale fakery uneconomic.
